q.t: The Sun appears to rise in the…
q.e: Because the Earth turns, the Sun appears to rise in the east and set in the west.

q.t: Does the Sun really move across the sky each day?
q.e: The Earth rotates once in about 24 hours.

q.t: The Earth spins once in about…
q.e: One rotation = one day.

q.t: The Earth goes round the Sun once in a…
q.e: One trip round the Sun takes a year.

q.t: A globe is a…
q.e: A ball-shaped model showing land and sea.

q.t: How much of the Earth is in daylight at any moment?
q.e: Light falls only on the half facing the Sun.

q.t: Varsha is the season of…
q.e: Varsha (Jun–Aug) brings heavy rain.

q.t: Vasanta is…
q.e: Vasanta (Feb–Apr): flowers bloom and new leaves appear.

q.t: Which village is called India's 'First Village of the Sunrise'?
q.e: It is the first Indian land the Sun's rays touch each morning.

q.t: The wettest inhabited place on Earth is…
q.e: India also has one of the driest places — the Thar Desert.

q.t: Why does the Sun seem to move when it's the Earth that turns?
o: We are standing on the thing that turns
q.e: Like trees seeming to slide backwards from a moving bus.

q.t: Why don't we feel the Earth spinning?
o: The turn is smooth and everything turns with us
It is too slow to exist
q.e: You only feel movement when something changes.

q.t: When it is day in India, it is night…
o: On the opposite side of the globe
q.e: The far half of the ball is in its own shadow.

q.t: Seasons happen because the Earth…
o: Is tilted as it travels round the Sun
q.e: Your half leans towards the Sun for part of the year, away for the rest.

q.t: Why do seasons repeat every year?
o: The journey round the Sun takes a year and starts again
q.e: A season is a position in a journey.

q.t: The monsoon is…
o: A wind that changes direction with the season
q.e: Moist air blows in from the sea in summer, out in winter.

q.t: Why does moist air blow inland in summer?
o: Land gets hotter than the sea
q.e: Land heats faster than water.

q.t: Pongal and Makar Sankranti are celebrated in winter because…
q.e: They are thanksgiving festivals after the harvest.

q.t: Holi is celebrated in…
q.e: Flowers bloom and the cold ends.

q.t: Why do scientists measure over time instead of trusting impressions?
o: Some changes are too slow or fast for us to notice
q.e: 'Nothing is changing' often means 'nothing changes at my speed'.

q.t: Why are coastal places milder than inland ones?
o: The sea warms and cools slowly
Inland is closer to the Sun
q.e: Inland places swing to fierce extremes.

q.t: Why is one side of a mountain range wet and the other dry?
o: Mountains force moist air up, so it rains on one side
q.e: Air drops its rain going up; little is left for the far side.

q.t: Why are so many festivals right after a harvest?
o: Food to spare, work finished, everyone free
q.e: Those three things must line up for a big celebration.

q.t: Animals behaving differently before rain are…
o: Reacting to changes in air, moisture and pressure
q.e: They react slightly earlier than people notice.

q.t: What makes a cycle a cycle?
o: The last step leads back to the first
q.e: So there is no end — and it repeats.

q.t: Why is a cycle useful to farmers?
q.e: Farmers can plan sowing months ahead.

q.t: Why does Dong see sunrise before western India?
o: It is closer to the Sun
q.e: The Earth rotates west to east, so the east meets the Sun first.

q.t: Winter in Kerala is mild while in Kashmir it's very cold mainly because…
o: Kashmir is much further north (and high)
q.e: How far north or south a place is changes its seasons.

q.t: Shishir is…
q.e: Shishir (Dec–Feb): cold, short days, mist and fog.

q.t: In winter the monsoon winds…
q.e: The land is cooler than the sea, so the wind direction flips.

q.t: A mountain rising and a valley deepening are invisible to us because…
q.e: Changes slower than our memory span become invisible.

q.t: An insect's wing flap is also hard to see because it is…
q.e: Changes much faster than our eyes can follow are missed too.

q.t: In the torch-and-globe demo, a sticker on India moves from the dark half into the light. That is…
q.e: Rotation carries you into the lit half — sunrise.

q.t: 'Change is not the opposite of order' means…
o: Nature's changes repeat so reliably we can build lives around them
q.e: In nature, the changing IS the order.

q.t: Sharad brings…
q.e: Sharad (Aug–Oct): rain eases, crops ripen.

q.t: Baisakhi, Vishu and Rongali Bihu mark…
q.e: A new farming year begins.

q.t: Why does it rain so much in India in one season rather than spread across the year?
o: The monsoon winds bring sea air only in summer
q.e: The seasonal reversal of winds gives a distinct rainy season.

q.t: A season is better described as…
o: A position in the Earth's journey round the Sun
q.e: That's why seasons are so reliable.

q.t: Birds migrating to the same place every year is an example of…
q.e: Cycles let birds return to a place they left a year ago.

q.t: Which is NOT a reason regions in India differ in seasons?
q.e: The three main reasons are latitude, the sea and mountains.
